Greetings, viewer from the future. You're probably here to look at this historic monument too. I'm writing this on 18 June 2015, about a week after "The Fattening" - also known as "The Reddit Wedding" - drove many otherwise placid Redditors and lurkers to seek a new home on the internet. Whether you're here as part of a school trip to study the past, as a serious researcher, or just as a casual tourist, I'd like to say hi to you all, and remind you that the recent exodus from Reddit to Voat has been driven by one simple thing: a desire to speak freely.

To speak - to communicate - is one of the traits that contributes to our humanity. It is in the sharing of ideas that we are fully human, and to restrict what we say in any way is to restrict our humanity. I am here today, as are many others, because we seek the fewest possible restrictions on what we say. All words have power, and each of us has the power to utter words of kindness, words of strength, words of goodness and gentleness and honor. Equally, we can give voice to words of woe, hatefulness and bitterness. We are here because we believe the repeated lesson of history, echoing from age to age and continent to continent: that attempts to restrict words of some kinds but not others inevitably leads to restrictions on words of all kinds. We believe that the free word is the tool of the free man, and that free speech is the foundation of a free society.

We are here, at this post, because this is the beginning. And in the beginning was the Word.

Good luck and free speech to you all.
